solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Arrived with reckless Yankee unwilling to be photographed

parts.note: came means arrived, in the past tense
rash means acting without care for consequences
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone turned up with a wild American who refused to have their picture taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera-shy person avoids cameras and dislikes posing for pictures.

clue.text: Put some power into attack

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... a battery, filling it with electricity
second meaning: to rush at an enemy

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one instruction to hit harder; the two halves are separate senses of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both loading a battery with electricity and rushing forward in an assault.

clue.text: Time to abandon Mr Scrooge?

indicators.note: to abandon says the letter for time leaves the title

parts.note: Mr is the short form of mister

explanation.surface: Is it time to leave Mr Scrooge behind?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr Scrooge' looks like the definition as a unit, but Mr is wordplay and Scrooge alone is the definition, an example hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge of Dickens's A Christmas Carol is the archetypal hoarder of money, a skinflint.

clue.text: Scold person selling fish

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Telling off a fishmonger.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach someone is to rebuke them or express disapproval.

clue.text: Happy with lectures rejigged for classroom stand-in

indicators.note: rejigged means rearranged, so the letters of happy and lectures are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written, the first half of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, the second half of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased that the lessons have been reorganised for a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is only a link joining the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply teacher is a temporary substitute covering for an absent regular teacher.

clue.text: Finally play organ for a period of time

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word play

parts.note: its last letter is the one taken
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: An instruction to end a performance on the church organ, for some length of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the musical instrument beside 'play'; here it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a twelve-month span of time.

clue.text: Average kind of music rewound

indicators.note: a tape that is rewound runs backwards, so the word for the music is read from its end

parts.note: rap is a style of music with rhythmic spoken lyrics

explanation.surface: A comment that some genre of music is middling, played on a tape running backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the normal or typical standard, as in 'below par' or 'on a par'.

clue.text: Group of soldiers also involved in scheme

indicators.note: involved in places the word for also inside the word for scheme

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
too means also

explanation.surface: A unit of troops is also caught up in a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a small military unit, a subdivision of a company.

clue.text: Scoundrel beginning to rescue aquatic creature

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the word rescue

parts.note: its opening letter is the one taken
an otter is a river-dwelling mammal

explanation.surface: A villain starts to save a water animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotter is a dated British word for a cad or a contemptible person.

clue.text: Storyteller with a model from the east

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left, so the word is backwards

parts.note: to model is to pose, as for an artist

explanation.surface: A narrator accompanied by a fashion model who has arrived from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author of fables such as the tortoise and the hare.

clue.text: Livestock initially lost by friendly agricultural worker

indicators.note: lost tells us that letter is dropped from the word for friendly

parts.note: pleasant means agreeable and friendly in manner

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word livestock

parts.note: its opening letter is the one removed

explanation.surface: An amiable farmhand whose animals have gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a poor smallholder or labourer who works the land.

clue.text: Grotesque sculpture of a gory leg destroyed

indicators.note: the phrase a gory leg is broken up and its letters rebuilt into a new word

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bloody limb wrecked to make a hideous carving.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargoyles are the grotesque carved figures on church roofs, often serving as waterspouts.

clue.text: By the sound of it, female animals sleep

indicators.note: this tells us the answer is spoken like the word for female animals but spelt differently

parts.note: does are female deer, rabbits and hares

explanation.surface: A note that female beasts seem to be having a snooze.
explanation.definitionFit: To doze is to nap lightly, a brief or shallow slumber.

clue.text: A doodler recreated mythical city

indicators.note: recreated means made again in a new form, so the letters of a doodler are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sketching idly has redrawn a legendary city.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the legendary city of gold sought by Spanish conquistadors in South America.

clue.text: Hot candle jumping is an Olympic event?

indicators.note: the letters of hot candle leap about into a new order, like sparks off a flame

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Leaping over a lit candle is jokingly proposed as a sport for the Games.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: the answer is a ten-part contest rather than a single event, though it is one Olympic medal.
explanation.definitionFit: The decathlon is a ten-discipline athletics contest held at the Olympic Games.

clue.text: Reportedly sketch board game piece

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the answer sounds like the word for sketch

parts.note: a draft is a rough sketch or outline

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be drawing a counter from a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is one of the round counters used in the game of draughts, or checkers.

clue.text: Nut bread we brought up

parts.note: bread is slang for money, cash

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: We served up nutty bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' suggests a loaf; it is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew is a kidney-shaped edible seed, eaten as a nut.

clue.text: Look over most of Bob's summerhouse

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first word above the next

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter from the name

parts.note: Bob, the name, with the 's read as is

explanation.surface: Someone inspects most of Bob's garden hut.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob's here is read as 'Bob is', so the 's joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small open garden pavilion, a kind of summerhouse giving a view.

clue.text: Some seafarers a long way off

indicators.note: only some of the letters of seafarers are used, a run sitting inside the word

parts.note: the answer sits inside this word, in sea-FAR-ers

explanation.surface: Some sailors are far from home.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar is an adverb meaning at or to a great distance.

clue.text: View alternatively found in place with a canal

indicators.note: found in says the short word sits inside the place name

parts.note: Panama is the Central American country famous for its canal
or is the word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A scene that might also be seen somewhere with a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, unbroken vista of a landscape.

clue.text: Friend in a fighter jet above capital of Oman

indicators.note: in a down clue, above places the jet over the letter that follows

parts.note: taken as written
the MiG is a Russian-built fighter aircraft

indicators.note: capital of means the first letter of the country name

parts.note: its opening letter is the one taken

explanation.surface: A pal is in a warplane flying over the Omani capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, used informally in English for a pal.

clue.text: Tree in Spanish resort cut down

indicators.note: cut down shortens the resort name by its last letter

parts.note: Palma is the capital of Majorca and a holiday resort

explanation.surface: A tree in a Spanish holiday town has been felled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' suggests felling the tree; it trims the resort's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm is a tropical tree with a crown of large fronds.

clue.text: Pig getting clean? That's nonsense!

parts.note: a hog is a pig
to wash is to clean

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of a pig getting itself clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash is rubbish talk; originally it meant kitchen swill fed to pigs.

clue.text: A thumbs-up online for uniform

parts.note: taken as written
a like is the thumbs-up approval given to a post on social media

explanation.surface: Someone gives an approving click online to a piece of clothing worn by a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' reads as a noun for clothing, but it is the adjective meaning the same throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are alike are similar or identical, i.e. uniform in character.

clue.text: Briefly accompanying comedian

indicators.note: briefly signals the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: with means accompanying, together alongside

explanation.surface: A comic who tags along for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: A wit is a clever, humorous person, so a joker or comic.

clue.text: Old Venetian mother with chocolate hugs police officer

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: hugs means the sweet wraps around the officer, holding it inside

parts.note: a Rolo is a brand of caramel-filled chocolate sweet
cop is slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: Mum holds a chocolate while embracing a policeman, all to describe a figure from old Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the thirteenth-century merchant from Venice famed for his travels to China.
